summary.value: The paper try to address the length volatility in long-form generation by proposing several methods. The reviewers raised concerns regarding the generalizability and technical nature of the proposed solution. The primary criticism is that SELB functions as a brute-force patch or rule-based intervention that relies heavily on task-specific structural markers and manually preset parameters. Reviewers noted a potential collusion between the benchmark and the method.

reviewer_concerns.value:
Addressed: 
The concern regarding repetition/quality degradation by providing n-gram and TTR results. They also provided a preliminary extension to free-form tasks, showing it can be adapted to tasks without explicit chapters.

Outstanding Concerns: 
While the rebuttal showed the method can work on free-form tasks, it still requires active, manual intervention in the decoding loop. This makes the method more of an inference-time engineering trick than a robust scientific solution. 
The fairness of baselines was not fully resolved: the paper compares a highly-tuned, constraint-aware decoding strategy against vanilla models without similar inference-time optimizations, making the performance gap less surprising and potentially overstating the contribution.
